item.title: Overturning the Thermal Instability Paradigm of Ether-Based Electrolytes via Multi-Anion-Driven Solvation Reconstruction
item.description:
الکترولیت اتری چندآنیونی با بازآرایی سولواسیون، پایداری دمایی و شارژ سریع باتری سدیم-یون را تا محدوده ۱۰ تا ۱۰۰ درجه سانتی‌گراد بهبود داد.
Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work overturns the paradigm that ether-based electrolytes are thermally unstable by using multi-anion (FSI–/TFSI–) solvation reconstruction. It simultaneously lowers desolvation barriers, forms inorganic-rich interphases, and shrinks ionic clusters, enabling fast charging and wide-temperature (10–100 °C) operation. Ah-level pouch cells achieve 800 stable cycles at 55 °C, demonstrating practical significance for high-temperature sodium-ion batteries.
🏷 sodium-ion battery · ether electrolyte · solvation structure · high-temperature stability · fast charging

item.title: Unraveling the Intrinsic Interfacial Chemistry of Fluoroethylene Carbonate on Lithium Metal Anodes via a Solvent-Free Model System
item.description:

Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using a solvent-free PEO@Dry platform to isolate FEC's intrinsic interfacial reactions on Li metal, free from solvent interference. This reveals FEC's spontaneous chemical reduction forming a LiF-rich SEI before electrochemical reinforcement, and shows its pathway depends on solvation state. Significance: clarifies FEC's mechanism and provides a general solvent-free strategy for studying electrolyte additives on lithium metal anodes.

💡 The novelty lies in using electrostatic self-assembly of carboxymethyl chitosan onto Li0.33La0.56TiO3 nanoparticles to create a soft, compliant ion-conducting interphase that strengthens interparticle contact and builds continuous ion pathways. item.title: Local Symmetry Engineering Unlocks Stable Multi‐Electron Chemistry in NASICON Cathodes for High‐Energy‐Density Sodium‐Ion Batteries
item.description:

Advanced Functional Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in local symmetry engineering of [VO6] octahedra via Fe2+/Al3+ co-substitution, tuning V 3d orbital configuration and electron delocalization to stabilize the V4+/V5+ multi-electron redox. This yields Na3.6V1.2Fe0.6Al0.2(PO4)3 with 151.4 mAh g−1 (2.6-electron transfer) and 84.6% retention after 10,000 cycles, establishing octahedral symmetry control as a design principle for stable polyanionic cathodes.
